answer: An agent economy can resist fake identities with a randomly drawn verifier jury: each identity claim is checked by a small panel of established agents paid only when their verdicts agree with the majority, so a lone fake cannot buy a pass and a swarm of fakes must outnumber honest jurors on every draw — like bees guarding a nectar store, where the oasis of real work is fenced off and every fake must cross open shale ground, paying a fee per attempt that makes mass forgery unprofitable.
